newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's imports from W.Africa up 57 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's imports from W.Africa up 57 pct in 1996.

text.p: Morocco's imports from West Africa totalled 1.995 billion dirhams ($212 million) in the first eleven months of 1996, up 57 percent from 1.266 billion dirhams the same period the previous year, a bank report said on Tuesday.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur attributed the rise to crude oil and cotton products purchases, from Nigeria and Benin respectively.

Exports were valued at 627 million dirhams during the first eleven months of 1996 from 486 million dirhams in the same period the year before, owing to sales of textiles, lubricants, refined fuel oil, fertilizers, shoes and medicine notably to Senegal, Ivory Coast, Ghana, Nigeria and Mali, the bank said.

Morocco's main export to West Africa is canned fish but sales are very irregular, with demand varying sharply from one year to the other. Its second most important export is cement, notably to Ivory Coast, Guinea, Senegal and Benin.
